prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove chosen proteins, through heterobifunctional PROTACs and through the cereblon-based mechanism of molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation remains the strongest candidate on chemical substance. A small molecule is designed to induce proximity between an E3 ligase and a target, so the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome system removes the protein. Pharmacology becomes event-driven and catalytic, and targets without a classical active site become reachable. The principle was demonstrated in 2001 by Sakamoto, Crews and Deshaies and has been confirmed for more than two decades by many independent laboratories, with ternary-complex structures and numerous clinical-stage degraders. The cereblon discovery by Handa and colleagues is the other half of the story: it explained why thalidomide and its analogues work and showed that a monovalent molecule can also induce degradation. A citation that covers both strands describes the modality as it actually exists. This is also the point where I have moved, as explained in the responses.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved yet, so clinical vindication is incomplete and the award could be called early. Attribution is crowded and a three-name limit leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim, each with a real claim. Pairing PROTACs and glues also joins two lineages that were discovered separately, and a single citation risks blurring that history. I judge these costs acceptable because the mechanism is well established, but they are real.

responses.point: Linke argues that dropping Handa would leave a prize describing only half the modality, and that Ciulli's omission is regrettable but defensible because VHL chemistry refined a concept Crews and Deshaies had already demonstrated.
responses.response: In round 1 I resisted this, and on reflection I think he is right. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs drug-like, but they refined a principle that was already shown. The cereblon identification was a new mechanistic discovery that converted an empirical drug class into a rational one. Judged by discovery rather than field prominence, which is the chair's own test, Handa belongs ahead of Ciulli in a three-name cap. I therefore change my third name from Ciulli to Handa.

responses.point: Aqvist says that without the glue strand the prize reads as a story about bifunctional linkers only, and that Ciulli is the best alternative third name only if the committee wants a prize about rational design instead of mechanism of action.
responses.response: This is the clearest statement of the choice, and I now take the mechanism-of-action reading. A citation limited to heterobifunctional design would be accurate but narrow, and it would ignore the fact that cereblon-based degraders are the ones in the clinic. I still regard Ciulli's omission as the weakest point of this configuration and would not call it a clean decision. I keep the citation wording explicit about two routes to degradation, so it does not claim that PROTACs and glues share one origin.

responses.point: Zou ranks base editing first with Liu alone, argues that B029 has an attribution problem and is more premature than a modality already treating patients, and accepts that B029 is the likelier consensus candidate.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution problem is the real weakness of B029 and that B047 has the earlier clinical readout. I do not think that makes B029 premature: its mechanism is settled and independently replicated, and clinical approval of a modality has not been our test for a discovery. My remaining doubt about B047 is its relation to the 2020 CRISPR prize. I also still see no reason to weigh B047 against B029 as a second part, since that would not repair the attribution problem. I keep B047 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Somfai uses the Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli trio and insists the citation stay on the heterobifunctional design principle, while saying approval should not be awaited.
responses.response: We agree on timing and on not waiting for an approval. I now differ on the third name. A citation confined to heterobifunctional design is cleaner on paper, but it would leave out the cereblon mechanism that explains why a drug used for decades works. I think the scientific record is better served by the broader citation, with its cost in history stated openly, than by a narrow one that omits a discovery of equal weight.

uncertainties: Whether one citation can cover PROTACs and cereblon-based glues without implying that they share a single origin.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I now favour Handa but regard Ciulli's omission as a real cost, and Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim are also left out.
How much weight the committee should give to the absence of an approved degrader drug; I give it little, but others reasonably weigh it more.
Whether B047 base editing would be treated as chemistry given the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict. I have no documented link to any credited name on the shortlist. My field of nucleotide metabolism and regulation of ribonucleotide reductase lies near the biology degraders target, but I have no tie to degrader candidates. My Academy membership is in the biological sciences class.
